tweets.text:
Thank you to everyone who joined us. For a full write-up of each session, read our event report:

ご来場いただいた皆さま、ありがとうございました。各セッションの内容は、開催レポートでもお読みいただけます。

sakana.ai/symposium-2026/ 🐟

To close, @hardmaru and @SchmidhuberAI discussed how the World Models paper came about, what has changed in the eight years since, and what it means to be a scientist in the age of AI. Moderated by @Stefania_Druga.

youtu.be/oG8Fvcv2g3o 🐟

最後はDavid HaとJürgen Schmidhuberの 対談。論文「World Models」誕生の経緯、それから8年で起きたこと、AI時代の科学者のあり方を語り合いました。

Robert Lange (@RobertTLange) walked through the AI Scientist from v1 to v3, including a paper co-written with v3 that was accepted at ALIFE 2026, and what it will take to build discovery systems that go beyond benchmark hill-climbing.

youtu.be/H1CnLNrtIf0 🐟

Robert Langeは、 AIサイエンティストのv1からv3までの歩みと、これからの展望を紹介しました。

Our Chief Scientist Takuya Akiba (@iwiwi) introduced Sakana Sawara, a new LLM series we are building from scratch at the RSI Lab, and explained why LLM development is a research race, not just a GPU race.

youtu.be/8FyCRDz30KE 🐟

チーフサイエンティストの秋葉拓哉は、RSI Labで ゼロから開発する新しい言語モデルシリーズ「Sakana Sawara」（仮称）を発表しました。

In his keynote, @SchmidhuberAI traced neural networks back to Gauss and Legendre around 1800, highlighted the Japanese researchers behind modern deep learning, and revisited his 1990 work on world models and artificial curiosity.

youtu.be/wgD6EJmRpWg 🐟

Jürgen Schmidhuber 教授による基調講演では、ニューラルネットワークの起源をガウスとルジャンドルにさかのぼり、深層学習を支えた日本の研究者の貢献、1990年の世界モデルと人工好奇心、フィジカルAIの未来を語りました。

David Ha (@hardmaru) opened with a simple idea: intelligence emerges from constraints. He traced how the 2018 World Models paper built on Schmidhuber's earlier work, and laid out Sakana AI's approach to AI sovereignty in Japan.

youtu.be/AkP2WuhmATk 🐟

David Haはオープニング 講演にて、「知能は制約から生まれる」という考えを起点に、論文「World Models」とSchmidhuber教授の研究とのつながり、日本のAI主権に向けたSakana AIの取り組みを語りました。

Sakana AI Symposium in Tokyo now on YouTube

The sessions on world models, LLMs, AI scientists, and Physical AI, from the Sakana AI team and our Chief Scientific Advisor, @SchmidhuberAI.

Full Report: sakana.ai/symposium-2026/

From ancient handwriting to AI-generated art! 📖✨
A Thai researcher in Japan is using AI to make centuries-old kuzushiji texts readable—and developing a model that aims to generate ukiyo-e-style images that more faithfully reflect Japanese culture! 🎨

A quick note on who we're looking for as we build out the security research team in Tokyo:

You don't need a traditional academic publication record to apply. We welcome strong hands-on backgrounds across systems/reliability (OS, kernels, compilers, SRE), blue-team operations, or AI agent research. Real-world incident write-ups, failure analyses, and open-source tools count just as much as papers.
